findings.description: A hypothetical large-explosion trap becomes one that blows up the island

contexts.japanese: 仕掛けを失敗すると、大爆発を起こすなどという物騒な罠でもない限り、な。
contexts.japanesePC: 仕掛けを失敗すると、大爆発を起こすなどという物騒な罠でもない限り、な。
contexts.japanesePS3: 仕掛けを失敗すると、大爆発を起こすなどという物騒な罠でもない限り、な。
contexts.WH: Unless messing up sets off a trap that blows up the island, of course.
contexts.MG: Unless messing up sets off a trap that blows up the island, of course.
contexts.UP: Unless messing up sets off a trap that blows up the island, of course.

MG.japanese: 仕掛けを失敗すると、大爆発を起こすなどという物騒な罠でもない限り、な。悩むだけ無駄だと思い、２つ並んだｌの、右側に決め、それを引き抜く。文字盤には、５文字が残された。
MG.translation: Unless messing up sets off a trap that blows up the island, of course. Thinking it a waste of time to sit here worrying, I decided on the rightmost "l" and pulled it out. Five letters remained in the word.

UP.japanese: 仕掛けを失敗すると、大爆発を起こすなどという物騒な罠でもない限り、な。悩むだけ無駄だと思い、２つ並んだｌの、右側に決め、それを引き抜く。文字盤には、５文字が残された。
UP.translation: Unless messing up sets off a trap that blows up the island, of course. Thinking it a waste of time to sit here worrying, I decided on the "l" on the right and pulled it out. Five letters remained in the word.

findings.sourceReading: Beatrice qualifies trial and error: unless there is some dangerous trap that causes a huge explosion when the mechanism is operated incorrectly. No affected target or extent is specified.
findings.alternative: A huge explosion might threaten a large area, and blows up the island could be hyperbolic joking. But the island is an added concrete target and scale, furnishing a specific destructive scenario where the Japanese leaves an unspecified dangerous explosion.

findings.description: Trying every combination becomes process of elimination

contexts.japanese: 総当りで試すことだって出来る。
contexts.japanesePC: ５文字が作れる組み合わせなど、決して多くはないのだ。総当りで試すことだって出来る。
contexts.japanesePS3: 総当りで試すことだって出来る。
contexts.WH: There can't be so many possible combinations of those letters.  I could use process of elimination.
contexts.MG: I could use process of elimination.
contexts.UP: I could use process of elimination.
contexts.note: Complete continuous three-witness source-first review and coherent boundary context in saved reports. Parent verified MG175 expanded tenth-twilight epitaph wording versus PS3 and originalPC164983/164985 arrival wording; not PC carryover. MG513 by/be typo verified against originalWH166338 and UP. MG.japanese:
この謎は、完全に妾の頭を混乱させた。
しかし、残された文字はたったの５文字しかない。５文字が作れる組み合わせなど、決して多くはないのだ。総当りで試すことだって出来る。とりあえず試そうと思い、まず１文字目のｕを引き抜く。……残るは４文字。ｄ、ｒ、ｌ、ｏ。
MG.translation: This riddle left me totally confused. However, there were only five letters left. There can't be too many possible combinations of those letters. I could use process of elimination. Thinking I'd play around with it, I pulled out the "u". ...There were four letters left. "d", "r", "l", and "o".

UP.japanese:
この謎は、完全に妾の頭を混乱させた。
しかし、残された文字はたったの５文字しかない。５文字が作れる組み合わせなど、決して多くはないのだ。総当りで試すことだって出来る。とりあえず試そうと思い、まず１文字目のｕを引き抜く。……残るは４文字。ｄ、ｒ、ｌ、ｏ。
UP.translation:
This riddle left me totally confused.
However, there were only five letters left. There can't be so many possible combinations of those letters. I could use process of elimination. Thinking I'd play around with it, I pulled out the "u". ......There were four letters left. "d", "r", "l", and "o".

findings.sourceReading: There are not many arrangements of five letters, so she could test every combination exhaustively.
findings.alternative: Exhaustive tests can eliminate failed arrangements one by one. Nonetheless process of elimination is a broader inference method and omits the actual proposed exhaustive testing, immediately followed by removing u to try possibilities.

findings.description: Hiding and feigning ignorance becomes hiding and forgetting the experience

contexts.japanese: 隠れて、知らん振りを決め込もうと心では思っても、足が動かない。
contexts.japanesePC: 隠れて、知らん振りを決め込もうと心では思っても、足が動かない。
contexts.japanesePS3: 隠れて、知らん振りを決め込もうと心では思っても、足が動かない。
contexts.WH: I thought about hiding and forgetting this ever happened, but my legs wouldn't move.
contexts.MG: I thought about hiding and forgetting this ever happened, but my legs wouldn't move.
contexts.UP: I thought about hiding and pretending this never happened, but my legs wouldn't move.
contexts.note: Complete continuous three-witness source-first review and coherent boundary context in saved reports. Parent verified MG175 expanded tenth-twilight epitaph wording versus PS3 and originalPC164983/164985 arrival wording; not PC carryover. MG513 by/be typo verified against originalWH166338 and UP. Inherited MG44 than/that pending. Ambiguous338 utterance direction, provisional463 and monetary-dream hyperbole513 limited516–520 held conservatively; no proven yellow additions.

MG.japanese: これほどの黄金を見つけたのだから、歓喜の声を上げるべきだと思った。……別に笑いたくはなかったが、このような場面では、そうするのが作法のように思い、無理やりにでも、笑ってみた。そんなだから、擦れた笑いが一つ二つ、口から零れただけだった。今となっては、歓喜の気持ちより、立ち入ってはならぬ場所に勝手に入ってしまったかのような、居心地の悪さの方が強い…。この、碑文の謎の終点で、妾はこれからどうすればいいのか、しばし呆然とする他なかった。その時、足音が近付いてくるのを聞いた。自分が下ってきた階段の方からだった。誰が来たのだろう。まさか、金蔵？このような場所にいることが知られたら、酷く叱られるのでは……。隠れて、知らん振りを決め込もうと心では思っても、足が動かない。妾は黄金の山の前で、……呆然と足音の人物がやって来るのを待ち受けていた…。
MG.translation: Considering the amount of gold I had just found, I figured I ought to be crying out in delight. ...I didn't really feel like laughing, but I thought it only good manners to do so in a situation like this, so I forced it out. Because of this, only a few feeble laughs slipped from my mouth. At that moment, even stronger than any delight was a feeling as though I'd entered a place I wasn't supposed to be... I couldn't think of what I should do next, now that the epitaph's riddle had been completed. Then, I heard approaching footsteps. It was coming from the stairway I had entered by. Someone was coming. Could it be...Kinzo? If he finds out I've been in a place like this, will I get scolded harshly...? I thought about hiding and forgetting this ever happened, but my legs wouldn't move. I kept standing there, stunned, in front of the pile of gold......as the footsteps drew closer and closer...

UP.japanese: これほどの黄金を見つけたのだから、歓喜の声を上げるべきだと思った。……別に笑いたくはなかったが、このような場面では、そうするのが作法のように思い、無理やりにでも、笑ってみた。そんなだから、擦れた笑いが一つ二つ、口から零れただけだった。今となっては、歓喜の気持ちより、立ち入ってはならぬ場所に勝手に入ってしまったかのような、居心地の悪さの方が強い…。この、碑文の謎の終点で、妾はこれからどうすればいいのか、しばし呆然とする他なかった。その時、足音が近付いてくるのを聞いた。自分が下ってきた階段の方からだった。誰が来たのだろう。まさか、金蔵？このような場所にいることが知られたら、酷く叱られるのでは……。隠れて、知らん振りを決め込もうと心では思っても、足が動かない。妾は黄金の山の前で、……呆然と足音の人物がやって来るのを待ち受けていた…。
UP.translation: Considering the amount of gold I had just found, I figured I ought to be crying out in delight. ......I didn't really feel like laughing, but I thought it only good manners to do so in a situation like this, so I forced it out. Because of this, only a few feeble laughs slipped from my mouth. At that moment, even stronger than any delight... was a feeling as though I'd entered a place I wasn't supposed to be... For a while, all I could do was stand there shocked, unsure what I should do now that the epitaph's riddle had been completed. Then, I heard approaching footsteps. They were coming from the stairway I had entered by. Someone was coming. Could it be...Kinzo? If he finds out I've been in a place like this, won't I get scolded harshly......? I thought about hiding and pretending this never happened, but my legs wouldn't move. I kept standing there, stunned, in front of the pile of gold......as the footsteps drew closer and closer...

findings.sourceReading: Fearing discovery and punishment, she intends to hide and resolutely pretend not to know anything, but cannot move.
findings.alternative: Forget this ever happened can idiomatically mean dismiss or conceal an experience. However, it omits the explicit performance of ignorance toward the approaching person, replacing that plan with forgetting.

findings.description: Permission for any solver becomes ability for anyone to solve

contexts.japanese: 碑文は、誰が解いても良かったはず。
contexts.japanesePC: 碑文は、誰が解いても良かったはず。私が解いても、おかしくはないはず......。
contexts.japanesePS3: 碑文は、誰が解いても良かったはず。
contexts.WH: Supposedly, anyone should have been able to solve the epitaph.  There shouldn't be anything strange about me solving it......
contexts.MG: Supposedly, anyone should have been able to solve the epitaph.
contexts.UP: It wasn't supposed to matter who solved the epitaph.
contexts.note: Complete continuous three-witness source-first review and coherent boundary context in saved reports. Parent verified MG175 expanded tenth-twilight epitaph wording versus PS3 and originalPC164983/164985 arrival wording; not PC carryover. MG513 by/be typo verified against originalWH166338 and UP. Inherited MG44 than/that pending. Ambiguous338 utterance direction, provisional463 and monetary-dream hyperbole513 limited516–520 held conservatively; no proven yellow additions.

MG.japanese: 熊沢も一緒だった。私の似合わないドレス姿を、色々と笑われるだろうと思っていたが、……彼女はまったく茶化さなかった。それどころか、私の姿を見て、……まるで、来るべき日がようやく来たとでも言うような、厳かな表情をしているのだった。……心臓が高鳴る。碑文は、誰が解いても良かったはず。私が解いても、おかしくはないはず……。源次たちは、ずっと神妙な顔をしていて、……これも含めて全てが、厳かな式典のようだった。息苦しい沈黙が、ずっと続く。やがて、扉が開き、源次が顔を覗かせた。
MG.translation: Kumasawa was with us too. I thought this dress, which didn't really suit me, would lead to a lot of jokes, ...but she didn't laugh at me at all. On the contrary, when she saw me, ...her expression had turned stern, as though a long-awaited day had finally come. ...My heart raced. Supposedly, anyone should have been able to solve the epitaph. There shouldn't be anything strange about me solving it... Genji and the others kept wearing serious expressions, ...and that, along with everything else, made this feel like some sort of grand ceremony. The suffocating silence continued. Eventually, the door opened, and Genji peeked out.

UP.japanese: 熊沢も一緒だった。私の似合わないドレス姿を、色々と笑われるだろうと思っていたが、……彼女はまったく茶化さなかった。それどころか、私の姿を見て、……まるで、来るべき日がようやく来たとでも言うような、厳かな表情をしているのだった。……心臓が高鳴る。碑文は、誰が解いても良かったはず。私が解いても、おかしくはないはず……。源次たちは、ずっと神妙な顔をしていて、……これも含めて全てが、厳かな式典のようだった。息苦しい沈黙が、ずっと続く。やがて、扉が開き、源次が顔を覗かせた。
UP.translation: Kumasawa was with us too. I thought this dress, which didn't really suit me, would lead to a lot of jokes, ......but she didn't laugh at me at all. On the contrary, when she saw me, ......her expression had turned stern, as though a long‐awaited day had finally come. ......My heart raced. It wasn't supposed to matter who solved the epitaph. There shouldn't be anything strange about me solving it...... Everyone else maintained solemn expressions, ......and that, along with everything else, made this feel like some sort of grand ceremony. The suffocating silence continued. Eventually, the door opened, and Genji peeked out.

findings.sourceReading: It should have been acceptable for anyone to solve the epitaph; therefore her solving it should not be inappropriate. The subject is eligibility, as she reacts to the unexpectedly solemn reception.
findings.alternative: Should have been able can sometimes imply permission, but anyone should have been able to solve a puzzle ordinarily asserts general capability. The next sentence partially preserves her concern without preserving the explicit permission claim.

findings.description: Avoiding an ordeal becomes avoiding making the family feel upset

contexts.japanese: 私は、そんな思いをしてまで当主になんかなりたくない。
contexts.japanesePC: 私は、そんな思いをしてまで当主になんかなりたくない。
contexts.japanesePS3: 私は、そんな思いをしてまで当主になんかなりたくない。
contexts.WH: I don't want to become the head if it means making them feel like that.
contexts.MG: I don't want to become the Head if it means making them feel like that.
contexts.UP: I don't want to become the head if it means making them feel like that.
contexts.note: Complete continuous three-witness source-first review and coherent boundary context in saved reports. Parent verified MG175 expanded tenth-twilight epitaph wording versus PS3 and originalPC164983/164985 arrival wording; not PC carryover. MG513 by/be typo verified against originalWH166338 and UP. Inherited MG44 than/that pending. Ambiguous338 utterance direction, provisional463 and monetary-dream hyperbole513 limited516–520 held conservatively; no proven yellow additions.

MG.japanese: 突然、右代宮家の当主は私なんてことになれば、蔵臼さまがどんな顔をなさるやら。奥様がどんな形相でお怒りになられるやら。私は、そんな思いをしてまで当主になんかなりたくない。私が何者か、今日、私は得ることが出来た。誰から、いつ、どのようにして生まれてきたのか。……それを、時間をかけてゆっくりと、彼らから聞いていこう。それだけで、もう、充分なのだ。
MG.translation: If I suddenly became the Ushiromiya Family Head, how would Krauss-sama react? How angry would Madam be? I don't want to become the Head if it means making them feel like that. Today, I learned who I am. Who gave birth to me, how, and when? ...These are things I want to learn from them as time goes by. That alone is enough.

UP.japanese: 突然、右代宮家の当主は私なんてことになれば、蔵臼さまがどんな顔をなさるやら。奥様がどんな形相でお怒りになられるやら。私は、そんな思いをしてまで当主になんかなりたくない。私が何者か、今日、私は得ることが出来た。誰から、いつ、どのようにして生まれてきたのか。……それを、時間をかけてゆっくりと、彼らから聞いていこう。それだけで、もう、充分なのだ。
UP.translation: If I suddenly became the Ushiromiya family head, how would Krauss‐sama react? How angry would Madam be? I don't want to become the head if it means making them feel like that. Today, I learned who I am. Who gave birth to me, how, and when? ......These are things I want to learn from them as time goes by. That alone is enough.

findings.sourceReading: She does not want to become head at the cost of undergoing such an experience: facing Krauss reaction and Natsuhi anger. そんな思いをして describes the speaker experiencing it.
findings.alternative: Their upset is the anticipated source of her ordeal, so the English shares the same situation. It nevertheless transfers the emotional cost from her undergoing it to her making them feel that way, changing the stated reason for refusal.

contexts.japanesePS3: ……私の中では、真の当主様は、あなただけでございます」

MG.japanese: 「畏まりました。ここに至る仕掛けも鍵も、全てあなただけのものでございます。……そして今夜のことは私共一同、秘密にすることを誓います。………次期当主は蔵臼さまとなられますが、……私の中では、真の当主様は、あなただけでございます」「……ご命令に従い、これからもこれまでと同じように振る舞いますが、いつでも御用命下さい。私の主は、あなただけなのでございます」

The device leading to this place and the key both belong to you. ...And all of us swear to keep the events of this night a secret. ...Krauss-sama will be the Successor, ...but in my heart, you will be the only true Successor." "...As you have ordered, we will behave the same way we always have, but please order us whenever it suits you. You are my only master."

UP.japanese: 「畏まりました。ここに至る仕掛けも鍵も、全てあなただけのものでございます。……そして今夜のことは私共一同、秘密にすることを誓います。………次期当主は蔵臼さまとなられますが、……私の中では、真の当主様は、あなただけでございます」「……ご命令に従い、これからもこれまでと同じように振る舞いますが、いつでも御用命下さい。私の主は、あなただけなのでございます」

The mechanism leading to this place and the key both belong to you. ......And all of us swear to keep the events of this night a secret. .........Krauss‐sama will be the successor, ......but in my heart, you will be the only true successor." "......As you have ordered, we will behave the same way we always have, but please order us whenever it suits you. You are my only master."

findings.sourceReading: Krauss will be the next head publicly, but Genji recognizes her alone as the true head now. Next head and true head are deliberately different titles.
findings.alternative: Successor fits inheritance vocabulary and Genji immediately calls her his only master. That preserves allegiance but does not make the title accurate: the source contrasts future public office with her present true authority.

findings.description: Past and future continuity becomes a qualified assessment of changes already made

contexts.japanese: 思えば、これまでとこれからも、何も変わらない。
contexts.japanesePC: 思えば、これまでとこれからも、何も変わらない。
contexts.japanesePS3: 思えば、これまでとこれからも、何も変わらない。
contexts.WH: If I think about it, not much has actually changed.
contexts.MG: If I think about it, not much has actually changed.

MG.japanese:
莫大な黄金の山と、右代宮家の当主の指輪。
肖像画のベアトリーチェのドレス。そして、………私は本当に、黄金の魔女、ベアトリーチェとなる。この、私だけの黄金郷で。思えば、これまでとこれからも、何も変わらない。だって私は最初から黄金の魔女で、……それが今、ほんの数人に、認められただけなのだから。１１月２９日。
私は本当の魔女に、なりました。
MG.translation:
A vast mountain of gold and the ring of the Ushiromiya Family Head. The dress of the portrait Beatrice. And, ...I became the true Beatrice, the Golden Witch. Right here in my very own Golden Land. If I think about it, not much has actually changed. After all, I've always been the Golden Witch. ......I've just had a few more people acknowledge that. November 29th. 
The day I became a true witch.

莫大な黄金の山と、右代宮家の当主の指輪。
肖像画のベアトリーチェのドレス。そして、………私は本当に、黄金の魔女、ベアトリーチェとなる。この、私だけの黄金郷で。思えば、これまでとこれからも、何も変わらない。だって私は最初から黄金の魔女で、……それが今、ほんの数人に、認められただけなのだから。１１月２９日。
私は本当の魔女に、なりました。
UP.translation:
A vast mountain of gold and the ring of the Ushiromiya family head.
The dress of the portrait Beatrice. And.........I became the true Beatrice, the Golden Witch. Right here in my very own Golden Land. If I think about it, not much has actually changed. After all, I've always been the Golden Witch. ......I've just had a few more people acknowledge that. November 29th.

findings.sourceReading: On reflection, nothing changes between before and from now on; she has always been the Golden Witch and has merely gained a few acknowledgments.
findings.alternative: Not much has changed is natural retrospective understatement, and the preceding explicit wish for continuity helps. But this sentence loses the explicit future comparison and weakens nothing into not much.

contexts.note: Exact active originalPC and paired prose directly checked under ep07-ep08-inherited-grammar-supplement-2026-10-13

MG.japanese:
不思議には思っても、それ以上のことは何も考えなかった。お館様の大事なレリーフだから、使用人頭の源次が自ら。……それで納得してしまっていた。しかし、今になれば納得できる。
やはり、このレリーフには仕掛けがあったのだ。それに不用意に近付かせないために、源次が自ら磨いていたのだ……。
MG.translation: I thought it strange, but nothing more. The Master treasured this relief, so the head servant cared for it himself. ...I always accepted that excuse. But now, I understand. There must be something in this relief. And Genji polished it himself to make sure than no one else accidentally found out...

UP.japanese:
不思議には思っても、それ以上のことは何も考えなかった。お館様の大事なレリーフだから、使用人頭の源次が自ら。……それで納得してしまっていた。しかし、今になれば納得できる。
やはり、このレリーフには仕掛けがあったのだ。それに不用意に近付かせないために、源次が自ら磨いていたのだ……。
UP.translation:
I thought it strange, but nothing more. The Master treasured this relief, so the head servant cared for it himself. ......I always accepted that excuse. But now, I understand.
There must be a trick to this relief. And Genji polished it himself to make sure that no one else accidentally found out......

findings.description: MG rewrites the epitaph arrival clue and its solution as a treasure-power exponent puzzle.

contexts.japanese: 旅は終わり、黄金の郷に至るだろう……。
contexts.japanesePS3: 旅は終わり、黄金の郷に至るだろう……。
contexts.MG: At journey's end, you shall attain to the power of the Golden Land's treasures, once and for the last time...
contexts.UP: The journey ends, and you shall reach the Home of the Gold......

MG.japanese:
これで、魔女は、……妾は蘇ったというのか……？第十の晩。
旅は終わり、黄金の郷に至るだろう……。何かを求め、はしごを降りて周りを見回した時。……すぐにその小さな変化に気が付いた。
MG.translation: So, this way, has the witch...have I...revived...? The tenth twilight. At journey's end, you shall attain to the power of the Golden Land's treasures, once and for the last time... When I stepped down off the ladder and looked around, ...I immediately noticed a small change.

UP.japanese:
これで、魔女は、……妾は蘇ったというのか……？第十の晩。
旅は終わり、黄金の郷に至るだろう……。何かを求め、はしごを降りて周りを見回した時。……すぐにその小さな変化に気が付いた。
UP.translation:
So now...has the witch...have I...revived......? The tenth twilight.
The journey ends, and you shall reach the Home of the Gold...... When I stepped down off the ladder and looked around, ......I immediately noticed that small change.

findings.sourceReading: The source concludes by reaching the Golden Land. CH16 explains 郷 read as kyou, then 京 interpreted as kei (10^16), one tenth giving quadrillion. MG adds treasure power and finality to the epitaph and replaces the Kyoto/kei reasoning with repeated exponentiation. Original PC163883/163977/164003 and164983/164985 preserve the Japanese chain and arrival; UP follows them.
findings.alternative: The English adaptation coordinates its altered epitaph with a solvable English mechanism. This explains the editorial choice but does not preserve the source clue, Rosa theory, or narrated arithmetic; it is one connected adaptation rather than multiple independent defects.
